title: Memory Recovery Promotion States — From Buried Trace to Canonical Use
purpose: Define the states through which recovered conversations, screenshots, files, recollections and archive fragments can move before they are reused by canonical owners.

states.meaning: A potentially relevant trace has been located but not authenticated or contextualized.
The trace is identified strongly enough to know what object/account/file it is.
The strongest defensible date or range is recorded with precision and basis.
Enough surrounding material survives to understand what the trace was responding to or doing.
Direct wording, paraphrase, recollection, reconstruction and later interpretation are separated.
Earlier/later sources, contradictions and developmental changes have been checked.
The trace materially deepens an existing canonical owner or timeline without needing a new owner.
The canonical owner has been updated while provenance and prior state remain traceable.
Unique source value remains, but substantive content has already been absorbed elsewhere.
Insufficient authenticity, excessive ambiguity, duplication or lack of relevance blocks promotion.

promotion_tests: Does this add a new fact, earlier attestation, clearer wording, stronger date, contradiction, mechanism or relationship?
Is there already a canonical owner that should absorb it?
Would promotion accidentally turn later interpretation into earlier wording?
Are quotations exact enough to publish as quotes?
Does the trace add independent provenance or merely repeat an existing root?
What becomes less certain if this trace conflicts with current canon?
Can the archive preserve the old state after revision?

recovery_batch_contract.success_rule: A recovery batch is successful when it improves source precision or developmental understanding, not when it maximizes the number of promoted items.

contradiction_outcomes.use_when: Both statements are well sourced but belong to different periods or roles.
One wording/date rests on materially stronger contemporaneous evidence.
Apparently conflicting claims refer to different domains, actors or meanings.
A later source explicitly retracts or corrects an earlier statement.
